name: Industrial Production
description: A seasonally adjusted index measuring the real output of the U.S. industrial sector, including manufacturing, mining, and electric and gas utilities. The index uses a reference period of 2017 = 100.
use: Monitor changes in U.S. industrial output and assess conditions across manufacturing, mining, and utility production.
purpose: Provide a broad measure of industrial-sector activity for analyzing economic momentum, production trends, business conditions, and changes in the business cycle.
significance: Industrial production provides information about real output in major industrial sectors of the U.S. economy. Changes in the index can help identify shifts in production activity and economic momentum, particularly within manufacturing and other industrial sectors.

name: Initial Jobless Claims
description: The number of initial claims for unemployment insurance filed by individuals following separation from an employer. The series is seasonally adjusted and reported weekly, with observations representing the week ending Saturday.
use: Monitor new unemployment insurance claims and identify changes in labor-market conditions, layoffs, and emerging weakness or strength in employment.
purpose: Provide a high-frequency measure of new unemployment insurance claims for analyzing labor-market conditions and detecting changes in employment trends before slower monthly indicators are released.
significance: Initial jobless claims provide a timely signal of new unemployment following job separations. Sustained changes in claims can provide information about labor-market conditions, layoffs, and shifts in economic activity.

name: Investment Grade Credit Spread
description: The ICE BofA U.S. Corporate Index Option-Adjusted Spread, measuring the spread between investment-grade U.S. corporate bonds and a comparable Treasury yield curve after adjusting for embedded options. The series is reported as a daily closing value and is not seasonally adjusted.
use: Monitor credit-market conditions and changes in the compensation investors demand for holding investment-grade corporate debt relative to U.S. Treasury securities.
purpose: Provide a market-based measure of investment-grade corporate credit spreads for analyzing credit risk, financial conditions, investor risk pricing, and changes in corporate bond markets.
significance: The investment-grade credit spread reflects the additional yield demanded by investors for investment-grade corporate debt relative to a Treasury reference curve. Changes in the spread can provide information about shifts in perceived credit risk, risk appetite, and broader financial-market conditions.

name: Job Openings
description: The number of available nonfarm jobs that remain unfilled on the last business day of the month and meet the criteria for an active job opening. The series is seasonally adjusted and reported in thousands of job openings.
use: Monitor unmet demand for labor and changes in the availability of job opportunities across the nonfarm economy.
purpose: Provide a measure of labor demand and job-market tightness for analyzing employment conditions, labor shortages, hiring demand, and changes in economic activity.
significance: Job openings provide information about demand for workers that has not yet been met through hiring. Changes in openings can indicate shifts in labor-market tightness, employer hiring demand, and the balance between available workers and available jobs.

name: Labor Force Participation Rate
description: The percentage of the civilian noninstitutional population that is either employed or actively looking for work. The series is seasonally adjusted and published monthly.
use: Monitor changes in labor-force participation and assess shifts in the share of the population engaged in the labor market.
purpose: Provide a core measure of labor-force engagement for analyzing labor-market conditions, economic activity, workforce availability, and longer-term demographic and economic trends.
significance: The labor force participation rate provides information about the share of the population working or actively seeking work. Changes in participation can affect the available labor supply and help distinguish changes in unemployment from changes in labor-force entry or exit.

name: M2 Money Supply
description: A broad measure of the U.S. money supply consisting of currency and deposits and other liquid assets included in the Federal Reserve's M2 monetary aggregate. The series is seasonally adjusted and reported in billions of dollars.
use: Monitor changes in the quantity of money circulating through the U.S. financial system and assess changes in liquidity and monetary conditions.
purpose: Provide a broad measure of the U.S. money supply for analyzing monetary conditions, liquidity, financial activity, and relationships between money growth and broader economic conditions.
significance: M2 provides a broad measure of money and liquid deposits available within the U.S. financial system. Changes in M2 can provide information about shifts in monetary and liquidity conditions and can be analyzed alongside inflation, interest rates, credit, and economic activity.

name: NASDAQ Composite
description: A market-capitalization-weighted index tracking more than 3,000 common equities listed on the NASDAQ Stock Market, including common stocks, American depositary receipts, real estate investment trusts, and tracking stocks. The series is reported as a daily closing index value and is not seasonally adjusted.
use: Monitor broad U.S. equity-market performance across companies listed on the NASDAQ and assess changes in market sentiment, risk appetite, and the performance of growth-oriented and technology-heavy segments of the equity market.
purpose: Provide a broad benchmark for NASDAQ-listed equities for analyzing equity-market conditions, investor risk appetite, market expectations, and changes across technology and growth-oriented portions of the U.S. stock market.
significance: The NASDAQ Composite provides broad exposure to equities listed on the NASDAQ Stock Market and includes companies across multiple industries, with substantial representation from technology and growth-oriented businesses. Changes in the index provide information about equity-market performance and investor expectations and can help contextualize broader financial-market conditions.

name: Natural Gas
description: The daily Henry Hub spot price of natural gas in U.S. dollars per million British thermal units (MMBtu), representing the benchmark price for natural gas delivered at Henry Hub in Louisiana.
use: Monitor U.S. natural gas prices and assess changes in energy supply and demand, weather-driven consumption, electricity generation, storage conditions, industrial activity, and energy-related inflation.
purpose: Provide a market-based measure of U.S. natural gas prices for analyzing domestic energy-market conditions, seasonal demand, electricity-generation costs, industrial energy demand, and changes in broader economic and inflationary conditions.
significance: Natural gas is an important U.S. energy commodity used for electricity generation, residential and commercial heating, and industrial processes. Henry Hub prices respond to changes in production, storage, weather, pipeline and infrastructure conditions, and demand from power generation and industry. Natural gas prices therefore provide signals about U.S. energy-market tightness, seasonal conditions, electricity costs, and energy-related inflation.

name: Nominal Advanced Foreign Economies U.S. Dollar Index
description: A trade-weighted index measuring the nominal value of the U.S. dollar against currencies of advanced foreign economies. The index is reported daily, is not seasonally adjusted, and uses January 2006 = 100 as its reference period.
use: Monitor changes in the U.S. dollar's nominal value against currencies of advanced foreign economies and assess exchange-rate conditions, international financial conditions, and cross-border economic relationships.
purpose: Provide a trade-weighted measure of the U.S. dollar against advanced-economy currencies for analyzing foreign-exchange conditions, relative currency movements, monetary policy transmission, and international financial conditions.
significance: The index isolates movements in the U.S. dollar relative to currencies of advanced foreign economies using trade-weighted exchange rates. Changes can provide information about dollar strength, international capital conditions, trade relationships, and differences in monetary and economic conditions across major advanced economies.

name: Nominal Broad U.S. Dollar Index
description: A trade-weighted index measuring the value of the U.S. dollar against a broad group of foreign currencies. The index is reported daily, is not seasonally adjusted, and uses January 2006 = 100 as its reference period.
use: Monitor changes in the broad nominal value of the U.S. dollar and assess foreign-exchange conditions, international financial conditions, trade competitiveness, and cross-border capital flows.
purpose: Provide a broad measure of U.S. dollar strength against major trading-partner currencies for analyzing foreign-exchange conditions, monetary policy transmission, global financial conditions, and relationships between the dollar and other asset markets.
significance: The broad U.S. dollar index provides a trade-weighted measure of changes in the dollar's value across a broad set of foreign currencies. Changes in the index can affect import prices, export competitiveness, international capital flows, commodity pricing, and global financial conditions.

name: Nominal Emerging Market Economies U.S. Dollar Index
description: A trade-weighted index measuring the nominal value of the U.S. dollar against currencies of emerging market economies. The index is reported daily, is not seasonally adjusted, and uses January 2006 = 100 as its reference period.
use: Monitor changes in the U.S. dollar's nominal value against currencies of emerging market economies and assess foreign-exchange conditions, global financial conditions, capital flows, and international economic relationships.
purpose: Provide a trade-weighted measure of the U.S. dollar against emerging-market currencies for analyzing foreign-exchange conditions, international financial conditions, monetary policy transmission, and changes in cross-border capital flows.
significance: The index measures movements in the U.S. dollar relative to currencies of emerging market economies using trade-weighted exchange rates. Changes in the index can provide information about dollar strength, emerging-market financial conditions, international capital flows, and differences in monetary and economic conditions across emerging markets.

name: Nonfarm Payrolls
description: The number of employees in the U.S. nonfarm economy, excluding proprietors, private household employees, unpaid volunteers, farm employees, and the unincorporated self-employed. The series is seasonally adjusted and reported in thousands of persons.
use: Monitor changes in total nonfarm employment and assess labor-market conditions, job creation, and changes in overall economic activity.
purpose: Provide a broad measure of U.S. employment for analyzing labor-market strength, economic growth, household income, business activity, and changes in the business cycle.
significance: Nonfarm payrolls are a major measure of U.S. employment and provide information about changes in the number of jobs across the economy. Sustained increases or decreases can provide insight into labor-market conditions and broader economic momentum.

name: NZD/USD
description: The daily exchange rate between the New Zealand dollar and the U.S. dollar, representing the value of one New Zealand dollar in U.S. dollars. The series provides daily open, high, low, and closing exchange rates.
use: Monitor NZD/USD movements and assess changes in New Zealand-U.S. monetary policy expectations, interest-rate differentials, currency strength, commodity and export conditions, Asia-Pacific economic activity, and global risk sentiment.
purpose: Provide a market-based measure of the New Zealand dollar against the U.S. dollar for analyzing New Zealand currency strength, New Zealand-U.S. interest-rate differentials, trade and export conditions, and changes in global market risk appetite.
significance: NZD/USD is a major foreign-exchange pair linking New Zealand and the United States. Changes in the exchange rate can reflect shifts in Reserve Bank of New Zealand and Federal Reserve policy expectations, interest rates, New Zealand's terms of trade and export prices, economic conditions in China and the Asia-Pacific region, capital flows, and global risk sentiment.

name: Personal Consumption Expenditures
description: A measure of spending by households on goods and services in the United States. The series is reported as a seasonally adjusted annual rate and expressed in billions of dollars.
use: Monitor household consumption and changes in consumer spending, a major component of U.S. economic activity.
purpose: Provide a broad measure of personal consumption expenditures for analyzing consumer demand, economic growth, household spending behavior, and broader economic conditions.
significance: Personal consumption expenditures represent a major component of U.S. economic activity. Changes in consumer spending can provide information about household demand, economic momentum, and shifts in consumption patterns.

name: Personal Income
description: The income received by individuals in the United States from labor, property, and capital, together with net current transfer payments received from businesses and government. The series is reported as a seasonally adjusted annual rate in billions of dollars.
use: Monitor changes in aggregate income received by households and assess household financial conditions, consumer spending capacity, and economic activity.
purpose: Provide a broad measure of personal income for analyzing household income conditions, consumer demand, savings, and changes in overall economic activity.
significance: Personal income captures income received by individuals from labor, assets, and transfers. Changes in personal income can provide information about household purchasing capacity and economic conditions and can help explain changes in consumer spending.

name: Producer Price Index
description: A monthly price index measuring changes in prices received by producers across all commodities in the United States. The index uses a reference period of 1982 = 100 and is not seasonally adjusted.
use: Monitor changes in prices received by producers across the broad commodity economy and assess producer-level price pressures.
purpose: Provide a broad measure of producer price movements for analyzing upstream inflation pressures, commodity pricing, production costs, and potential changes in consumer prices.
significance: The Producer Price Index provides information about price changes at the producer level before goods and services reach consumers. Changes in producer prices can provide insight into upstream inflation pressures and changes in production costs.

name: Real 10-Year Treasury Yield
description: The market yield on 10-year U.S. Treasury securities whose principal and interest payments are adjusted for inflation. It represents a market-based measure of the real interest rate for a 10-year maturity.
use: Monitor real long-term interest rates and assess changes in inflation-adjusted borrowing costs, financial conditions, and market expectations.
purpose: Provide a market-based measure of the real 10-year U.S. interest rate for analyzing real borrowing costs, inflation-adjusted returns, monetary policy, and financial conditions.
significance: The real 10-year Treasury yield provides information about the inflation-adjusted cost of long-term capital and the pricing of inflation-indexed government securities. Changes in the yield can affect financial conditions and the relative attractiveness of real versus nominal assets.

name: Real Broad U.S. Dollar Index
description: A trade-weighted index measuring the inflation-adjusted value of the U.S. dollar against a broad group of foreign currencies. The index is reported monthly, is not seasonally adjusted, and uses January 2006 = 100 as its reference period.
use: Monitor changes in the inflation-adjusted value of the U.S. dollar and assess international price competitiveness, trade conditions, and global financial conditions.
purpose: Provide a broad measure of the real, trade-weighted value of the U.S. dollar for analyzing exchange-rate competitiveness, international trade conditions, inflation-adjusted currency valuation, and relationships between the dollar and global economic conditions.
significance: The real broad dollar index accounts for relative price-level differences in addition to exchange-rate movements. Changes in the index can provide information about the inflation-adjusted competitiveness of U.S. goods and services and the broader international financial position of the dollar.

name: Real GDP Growth
description: The quarterly percentage change in inflation-adjusted U.S. gross domestic product from the preceding period, reported at an annual rate. The series is seasonally adjusted and measures changes in real economic output.
use: Monitor the pace of change in inflation-adjusted U.S. economic output and identify periods of economic expansion, slowing growth, or contraction.
purpose: Provide a published measure of quarterly real GDP growth for analyzing economic momentum, business-cycle conditions, and changes in aggregate economic activity.
significance: Real GDP growth measures changes in inflation-adjusted economic output and provides a broad indicator of economic momentum. Changes in the growth rate can help identify shifts between stronger and weaker periods of economic activity and changes in the business cycle.

name: Real Gross Domestic Product
description: The inflation-adjusted value of goods and services produced by labor and property located in the United States. The series is seasonally adjusted at an annual rate and reported in billions of chained 2017 dollars.
use: Monitor the inflation-adjusted level of U.S. economic output and assess changes in overall economic activity and growth.
purpose: Provide a broad measure of real U.S. economic output for analyzing economic growth, business-cycle conditions, productivity, and changes in aggregate economic activity.
significance: Real GDP measures the inflation-adjusted value of goods and services produced in the U.S. economy. Changes in real GDP provide a broad measure of economic expansion or contraction and are central to assessing overall economic conditions and the business cycle.

name: Reserve Balances
description: The average level of reserve balances held by depository institutions at Federal Reserve Banks during the week ending Wednesday. The series is not seasonally adjusted and is reported in millions of U.S. dollars.
use: Monitor the level of reserve balances held by depository institutions at Federal Reserve Banks and assess changes in banking-system liquidity and monetary conditions.
purpose: Provide a measure of reserve balances within the U.S. banking system for analyzing Federal Reserve balance-sheet operations, liquidity conditions, and the implementation of monetary policy.
significance: Reserve balances represent funds that depository institutions hold at Federal Reserve Banks. Changes in reserve balances provide information about banking-system liquidity and can help interpret the effects of Federal Reserve balance-sheet operations and broader monetary conditions.

name: Retail Sales
description: Seasonally adjusted monthly sales for U.S. retail trade and food services, reported in millions of dollars. The most recent observation is an advance estimate based on a subsample of firms and is subject to revision.
use: Monitor consumer spending activity through changes in retail trade and food-service sales and identify shifts in consumer demand and economic momentum.
purpose: Provide a timely measure of nominal retail and food-service sales for analyzing consumer demand, household spending, economic activity, and changes in consumption trends.
significance: Retail sales provide a timely signal of consumer demand and economic activity. Changes in sales can indicate shifts in household spending behavior and economic momentum, although the latest observation is an advance estimate and may be revised as more complete survey data become available.

name: Reverse Repo Usage
description: The aggregated daily amount of overnight reverse repurchase agreement transactions conducted by the Federal Reserve with eligible counterparties. The series is not seasonally adjusted and is reported in billions of U.S. dollars.
use: Monitor usage of the Federal Reserve's overnight reverse repurchase facility and assess changes in short-term liquidity and money-market conditions.
purpose: Provide a measure of overnight reverse repo activity for analyzing Federal Reserve open-market operations, money-market liquidity, reserve conditions, and changes in short-term financial conditions.
significance: Reverse repo usage reflects the amount of funds placed into the Federal Reserve's overnight reverse repurchase facility by eligible counterparties. Changes in usage can provide information about money-market conditions, the distribution of liquidity, and the interaction between Federal Reserve operations and short-term interest rates.

name: Russell 2000 Index
description: A daily measure of the Russell 2000 Index, a benchmark for U.S. small-cap equities, reported through Financial Modeling Prep. The indicator provides daily open, close, absolute change, and percentage change for the index.
use: Track daily movements in the Russell 2000 Index, including opening level, closing level, absolute price change, and percentage change, to monitor U.S. small-cap equity-market conditions.
purpose: Provide visibility into the performance and short-term direction of U.S. small-cap equities as a distinct segment of the broader U.S. stock market.
significance: The Russell 2000 is a widely used benchmark for U.S. small-cap equities and provides a different market perspective from large-cap indexes such as the S&P 500 and technology-heavy indexes such as the Nasdaq-100. Movements in the index can provide context for investor risk appetite, domestic economic expectations, financial conditions, credit conditions, and the relative performance of smaller U.S. companies. Because smaller companies can be more sensitive to domestic economic activity and financing conditions, Russell 2000 performance can complement broader equity-market indicators when analyzing U.S. market conditions and risk sentiment.

name: S&P 500
description: A market-capitalization-weighted index of 500 leading publicly traded U.S. companies across major industries, representing a broad measure of the large-cap U.S. equity market. The series is reported as a daily closing index value and is not seasonally adjusted.
use: Monitor broad U.S. equity-market performance and assess changes in investor risk appetite, financial conditions, market expectations, and the valuation of large-cap U.S. companies.
purpose: Provide a broad benchmark for U.S. large-cap equity markets for analyzing financial-market conditions, risk sentiment, economic expectations, and relationships between equity markets and macroeconomic indicators.
significance: The S&P 500 is a widely followed benchmark for the U.S. large-cap equity market. Changes in the index provide information about equity-market performance and investor expectations and can help contextualize broader financial conditions and risk sentiment. The series is a price index and does not include dividends or represent total return.

name: Silver
description: The daily market price of silver quoted in U.S. dollars per troy ounce, representing the prevailing value of silver in global commodity and financial markets.
use: Monitor silver prices and assess changes in industrial demand, economic activity, investment demand, monetary conditions, precious-metals sentiment, and demand from technology and clean-energy applications.
purpose: Provide a market-based measure of silver prices for analyzing precious-metals markets, industrial activity, investment demand, economic conditions, and changes in the balance between financial and industrial drivers of commodity demand.
significance: Silver has a dual role as both a precious metal and an industrial input, making its price sensitive to financial-market conditions as well as the global economic cycle. Demand from electronics, photovoltaics, automotive applications, power infrastructure, and other technologies connects silver prices to industrial activity, while investment demand and monetary conditions connect the metal to broader financial markets.

name: Solana Spot ETF Market
description: A daily measure of U.S. spot Solana ETF market activity, including aggregate net capital flows, traded value, net assets, and cumulative net flows. The indicator provides a view of capital entering or leaving Solana spot ETF vehicles and the size and activity of regulated investment products providing traditional investors with access to Solana.
use: Track daily capital flows, trading activity, assets under management, and cumulative capital flows in the U.S. spot Solana ETF market.
purpose: Provide a daily view of traditional-finance and institutional market participation in Solana through regulated spot ETF vehicles and identify changes in capital allocation toward Solana.
significance: Solana spot ETF market data provides a view of capital flows and asset levels within regulated investment vehicles that give traditional investors access to Solana. Net flow measures the daily net movement of capital into or out of the ETF market, while value traded measures ETF trading activity. Net assets indicate the aggregate size of assets held through the ETF vehicles, and cumulative net flow tracks the longer-term accumulation of capital flows. Solana ETF activity can provide context for traditional-finance participation in Solana and can be analyzed alongside Solana price, network activity, transaction activity, staking, DeFi activity, decentralized applications, stablecoin activity, derivatives positioning, macroeconomic conditions, liquidity conditions, and broader crypto-market sentiment. ETF flows should be interpreted as activity within the spot Solana ETF market and should not be treated as a complete measure of all institutional Solana ownership or total Solana demand.

name: U.S. National Home Price Index
description: The S&P Cotality Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price Index, a monthly measure of U.S. residential property values based on repeat-sales pricing of existing single-family homes. The index is not seasonally adjusted and uses January 2000 = 100 as its reference period.
use: Monitor changes in U.S. residential property values and assess trends in home prices, housing-market conditions, household wealth, and housing affordability.
purpose: Provide a broad measure of national U.S. home-price levels for analyzing housing-market trends, changes in property values, household wealth, and relationships between housing prices, financing costs, income, and economic conditions.
significance: The national home price index provides information about changes in residential property values across the United States. Changes in home prices can affect housing affordability, household wealth, housing demand, construction incentives, and broader economic conditions.

name: Unemployment Rate
description: The percentage of the U.S. civilian labor force that is unemployed. This series represents the U-3 measure of labor underutilization and is seasonally adjusted.
use: Monitor labor market conditions and changes in the share of the labor force that is unemployed.
purpose: Provide a core measure of U.S. labor market conditions for analyzing employment, economic activity, monetary policy, household conditions, and changes in the business cycle.
significance: The unemployment rate is a widely used measure of labor market conditions and economic slack. Changes in unemployment can provide information about labor-market strength, household income conditions, economic activity, and the broader business cycle.

name: USD/CAD
description: The daily exchange rate between the U.S. dollar and Canadian dollar, representing the value of one U.S. dollar in Canadian dollars. The series provides daily open, high, low, and closing exchange rates.
use: Monitor USD/CAD movements and assess changes in U.S.-Canadian monetary policy expectations, interest-rate differentials, Canadian dollar strength, commodity prices, energy markets, and North American financial conditions.
purpose: Provide a market-based measure of the exchange rate between the U.S. dollar and Canadian dollar for analyzing relative currency strength, U.S.-Canadian interest-rate differentials, commodity-driven economic conditions, and changes in cross-border financial markets.
significance: USD/CAD is a major foreign-exchange pair linking the United States and Canada. Changes in the exchange rate can reflect shifts in Federal Reserve and Bank of Canada policy expectations, interest rates, Canadian commodity prices and export conditions, particularly energy, trade flows, and broader North American economic and market conditions.

name: USD/CHF
description: The daily exchange rate between the U.S. dollar and Swiss franc, representing the value of one U.S. dollar in Swiss francs. The series provides daily open, high, low, and closing exchange rates.
use: Monitor USD/CHF movements and assess changes in U.S.-Swiss monetary policy expectations, currency strength, interest-rate differentials, and global risk sentiment.
purpose: Provide a market-based measure of the exchange rate between the U.S. dollar and Swiss franc for analyzing relative currency strength, U.S.-Swiss interest-rate differentials, monetary policy expectations, and cross-border financial conditions.
significance: USD/CHF is a major foreign-exchange pair linking the United States and Switzerland. Changes in the exchange rate can reflect shifts in relative economic conditions, Federal Reserve and Swiss National Bank policy expectations, interest rates, capital flows, and demand for the Swiss franc during changes in global risk conditions.

name: USD/JPY
description: The daily exchange rate between the U.S. dollar and Japanese yen, representing the value of one U.S. dollar in Japanese yen. The series provides daily open, high, low, and closing exchange rates.
use: Monitor USD/JPY movements and assess changes in U.S.-Japan monetary policy expectations, currency strength, interest-rate differentials, and broader global financial conditions.
purpose: Provide a market-based measure of the exchange rate between the U.S. dollar and Japanese yen for analyzing relative currency strength, U.S.-Japan interest-rate differentials, monetary policy expectations, and cross-border financial conditions.
significance: USD/JPY is a major foreign-exchange pair linking the United States and Japan. Changes in the exchange rate can reflect shifts in relative economic conditions, Federal Reserve and Bank of Japan policy expectations, interest rates, capital flows, and global risk sentiment.

name: WTI Crude Oil
description: The daily price of West Texas Intermediate crude oil in U.S. dollars per barrel. WTI is a light, sweet crude oil benchmark associated with physical crude traded and delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma.
use: Monitor U.S. crude oil prices and assess changes in global and domestic oil supply and demand, U.S. production, inventories, energy-market conditions, inflation pressures, economic activity, and geopolitical risks affecting oil markets.
purpose: Provide a market-based measure of U.S. crude oil prices for analyzing energy-market conditions, petroleum supply and demand, U.S. production and inventories, inflationary pressures, and the relationship between oil markets and broader economic conditions.
significance: WTI is a major crude oil benchmark and an important reference price for U.S. petroleum markets. Its price reflects changing expectations around crude oil supply and demand, U.S. production and inventories, refinery activity, transportation constraints, and global energy conditions. Because oil is a major input into transportation, manufacturing, and other economic activity, WTI movements can also provide signals about inflation and broader economic conditions.

name: XRP Spot ETF Market
description: A daily measure of U.S. spot XRP ETF market activity, including aggregate net capital flows, traded value, net assets, and cumulative net flows. The indicator provides a view of capital entering or leaving XRP spot ETF vehicles and the size and activity of regulated investment products providing traditional investors with access to XRP.
use: Track daily capital flows, trading activity, assets under management, and cumulative capital flows in the U.S. spot XRP ETF market.
purpose: Provide a daily view of traditional-finance and institutional market participation in XRP through regulated spot ETF vehicles and identify changes in capital allocation toward XRP.
significance: XRP spot ETF market data provides a view of capital flows and asset levels within regulated investment vehicles that give traditional investors access to XRP. Net flow measures the daily net movement of capital into or out of the ETF market, while value traded measures ETF trading activity. Net assets indicate the aggregate size of assets held through the ETF vehicles, and cumulative net flow tracks the longer-term accumulation of capital flows. XRP ETF activity can provide context for traditional-finance participation in XRP and can be analyzed alongside XRP price, XRP Ledger activity, transaction activity, payment and settlement use cases, cross-border payment infrastructure, derivatives positioning, macroeconomic conditions, liquidity conditions, and broader crypto-market sentiment. ETF flows should be interpreted as activity within the spot XRP ETF market and should not be treated as a complete measure of all institutional XRP ownership or total XRP demand.
